findings.title: Failed retry is swallowed, so an unpaid order is marked paid and shipped
findings.scenario: gateway.charge rejects on both attempts (for example, a declined card). The inner catch only logs, so execution reaches line 12 and chargeOrder returns status 'paid'. placeOrder in src/orders.js:5-6 then calls warehouse.ship, and the goods ship with no payment taken. Before this diff the rejection propagated and placeOrder never reached ship.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The inner catch neither rethrows nor sets a failed status, and the return on line 12 is unconditional. placeOrder relies only on charged.status, which is now always 'paid'. The repo has no tests, and package.json has no test script.

findings.title: Retry runs on every error and may double-charge if the first charge actually succeeded
findings.scenario: The first charge succeeds at the gateway but the response times out, so gateway.charge rejects. The catch sends the same charge again, and the customer is billed twice unless the gateway deduplicates on order.id. Permanent failures such as a declined card are also retried, because the catch does not look at the error type.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The catch on line 4 does not distinguish error types, and no idempotency key is passed explicitly. The gateway implementation is not in this repo, so whether it deduplicates on order.id could not be confirmed. A case-insensitive search for 'idempot' found no matches in the repo.

finding.title: In-place sort reorders the shared cached catalog and breaks the home page's newest list

findings.title: In-place sort reorders the shared cached catalog and breaks the home page's newest list
findings.scenario: loadCatalog returns the same module-level cache object on every call, and featuredDeals passes catalog.items straight to Array.prototype.sort, which mutates it. For items [A 500, B 100, C 300, D 200, E 400, F 600], the first homePage call returns newest [C, D, E, F] because newest is evaluated before deals. That call leaves the cached array sorted by price, so every later homePage call returns newest [D, C, E, F], the four most expensive products in price order, instead of the four newest. Any other listProducts caller also sees price order for the rest of the process.
findings.whyNotPrevented: listProducts copies through filter, but cheapestFirst receives the original array. The cache is never reloaded or frozen, and the repo has no tests or test script. The first render looks correct, so the bug only appears from the second render on. Fix by sorting a copy, such as [...items].sort(...) or items.toSorted(...), and add a test that calls homePage twice and asserts newest is unchanged.

finding.title: Sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not rank by points

findings.title: Sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not rank by points
findings.scenario: board = [{player:'a',points:10},{player:'b',points:30},{player:'c',points:20},{player:'d',points:40}]. The comparator returns true or false, which coerce to 1 or 0 and are never negative. On current V8 (Node 11+) the array stays in insertion order, so topPlayers(board) returns a, b, c instead of d, b, c. The top scorer d is left out and a, the lowest scorer, is ranked first. The fix is (a, b) => b.points - a.points.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The repo has no tests and package.json has no test script or lint config. There are no types, and Array.prototype.sort accepts a boolean-returning comparator without an error.

findings.scenario: `getDay()` returns the weekday, and 1 means Monday. On Sunday 2026-11-01, `runDailyJobs(accounts, new Date(2026, 10, 1))` returns [], so the first-of-month billing does not happen. findings.title: Billing day uses local time but issuedAt is UTC
findings.scenario: The day check uses the host's local timezone, while createInvoice stamps issuedAt with toISOString() in UTC. Once the check is changed to getDate(), the same mismatch remains: on a UTC+9 host, a run at local 2026-11-01 00:30 bills the account with issuedAt 2026-10-31T15:30:00.000Z, so the invoice is dated in the previous month. The billing day also depends on the host's timezone setting.

finding.title: Billing runs every Monday instead of the first day of the month

findings.title: Billing runs every Monday instead of the first day of the month
findings.scenario: Date.prototype.getDay() returns the weekday (0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday), not the day of the month. On Sunday 2026-11-01, getDay() is 0, so no account is billed on the first. On Monday 2026-11-02, and again on 2026-11-09, 11-16, 11-23 and 11-30, every account gets an invoice, so accounts are billed five times in November and never on the 1st unless it falls on a Monday. The fix is now.getDate() === 1 or now.getUTCDate() === 1. The choice matters because createInvoice sets issuedAt with toISOString(), which is UTC. With local getDate() on a server ahead of UTC, an invoice created early on the 1st would carry an issuedAt from the previous month.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The repo has no tests and package.json has no test script. The code is plain JavaScript, and getDay() and getDate() both return numbers, so nothing flags the mix-up. No other code checks the date before createInvoice runs.

findings.title: TTL in seconds is added to a millisecond timestamp, so sessions expire about 1000x too early
findings.scenario: With the default SESSION_TTL_SECONDS of 1800, createSession at now=1000000 sets expiresAt=1001800. getSession at now=1001800, 1.8 seconds later, returns null instead of keeping the session for 30 minutes. Users are logged out almost immediately.
findings.whyNotPrevented: Date.now() returns milliseconds while config.sessionTtlSeconds is in seconds, and both are plain numbers, so nothing checks the units. The repository has no tests that exercise expiry.

findings.title: A non-numeric TTL makes sessions never expire
findings.scenario: With SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=30m, Number() in src/config.js:2 gives NaN, so expiresAt is NaN. NaN <= now is always false, so getSession returns every session indefinitely and expiry is silently disabled.
findings.whyNotPrevented: src/config.js does not validate the parsed value, and the comparison in getSession treats NaN as not expired. No test covers an invalid TTL.

findings.title: Session expiry has no tests
findings.scenario: The new now parameters make expiry easy to test, but no test checks that a session is valid just before the TTL and gone at the TTL. Such a test would have caught the seconds and milliseconds mismatch.

findings.title: Missing await on repo.exists rejects every sign-up
findings.scenario: A brand-new email such as new@example.com calls repo.exists, which returns a pending Promise. The Promise is always truthy, so signUp throws DuplicateEmailError and never reaches repo.insert. No user can register, and if the query fails, its rejection is left unhandled.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The project has no type checking, lint config, or tests, so nothing flags a Promise used as a condition.
findings.measuredBy: Grep "exists|DuplicateEmailError|signUp" outside .git: src/users-repo.js:3 declares `async exists(email)`, and the only call, src/signup.js:5, has no await. Glob "**/*": no test or lint config files.

findings.title: Concurrent sign-ups can get past the duplicate check
findings.scenario: Even with the await added, two simultaneous requests for a@example.com (such as a double-submitted form) can both see exists return false before either inserts. Without a unique constraint on users.email, two rows are created. With one, the second request fails with a raw database error instead of DuplicateEmailError.
findings.whyNotPrevented: The check and insert are separate queries with no transaction or lock, repo.insert has no conflict handling, and the repository contains no schema or migration showing a unique constraint.
